title: W11 never pins the shed to the shared uplink — drops on the host's wide drop would pass the test
detail: The test's named contract is 'the shared standard uplink sheds', but assertions only prove drops>0 plus zero narrow-bundle drops. All drops could land on the host's wide drop (pipe 12) and it still passes.
recommended_fix: After the run, resolve bundle_of_pipe(&s, 13) and assert its by_bundle count > 0, pinning the shed to the shared uplink itself rather than any non-narrow bundle.

title: 5.10 health_test re-pin comments disagree on landing-tick arithmetic (sum vs sum+1)
evidence:
step_n(&s, 190, cat) // tick 250: the burst slid out at ~236 -> the latch EXITED
...
	// burn window after it is 288..351 = 63 ticks — the countdown must resume
	// from the burnt value, never re-arm (after <= after_exit - 20).
	step_n(&s, 100, cat)
...
	step_n(&s2, 170, cat) // tick 411: the expiry fired (~407), the meter is DRAINING (~92)
detail: Identical step patterns get contradictory annotations: 60+190 → 'tick 250' (plain sum) but 250+100 → '…351' and 240+170 → 'tick 411' (sum+1). At most one convention is correct; some annotation is off by one.
recommended_fix: Recompute the landing ticks (240+170=410; 250+100=350) or state step_n's inclusive/exclusive convention once, then align every re-pinned comment to it.

title: W11 aggregation pin never asserts the drops land ON the shared uplink bundle — the host's wide drop (pipe 12) is an unexcluded drop site
detail: Card hard req 3: "an aggregation scenario where the shared link (not the access drop) congests." The pin excludes only the 12 narrow bundles (pipes 0..11); drops>0 is global, so a shed at the host's wide drop (pipe 12) would satisfy it without the shared link congesting.
recommended_fix: Resolve the shared uplink's bundle (bundle_of_pipe(&s, 13)) and assert by_bundle[shared] > 0 alongside narrow_drops == 0. Test-only change; no golden churn.

recommended_fix: Update lines 233, 291, 295 to '(narrow 10 + wide 40)' / '(10+40)' — comment/message text only, no golden churn.

title: W11 port-budget comment miscounts the b-side — rb runs at exactly 8/8, not 7
evidence:
// the shared link is). router_mid ports: 6 res + uplink = 7 <= 8 per side.
...
	sla_draw(&s, cat, host, rb, "wide", 1)   // pipe 12 — the host drop
	sla_draw(&s, cat, ra, rb, "standard", 1) // pipe 13 — the shared uplink
detail: The '6 res + uplink = 7' arithmetic holds only for ra; rb carries 6 res drops + the host wide drop + the shared uplink = 8 incident pipes = exactly port_capacity 8, leaving no spare. The comment misleads future fixture edits (a new rb leg would be rejected).
recommended_fix: Correct the comment to note the b-side is 6 res + host + uplink = 8/8 (at capacity).
